 (x)clusive!: izna Set the Tempo with Their WHO DAT GIRL? Concert in Singapore
 Nov 15, 2026 sgx team 
 Reviews   (x)clusive stories 
 Singapore NAYAs finally got to spend an evening with izna as the six-member girl group brought their WHO DAT GIRL? concert tour to Capitol Theatre on 8 November 2026 and if anyone was wondering whether a group that debuted only in 2024 could keep a theatre full of fans entertained, the answer was a pretty enthusiastic yes!
 Formed through the survival programme I-LAND 2 , Mai , Jeemin , Koko , Sarang , Jungeun and Saebi have already built up a collection of songs that fans know by heart. Their first headlining concert in Singapore was a chance to hear those favourites live, but it was also an opportunity to get to know the personalities behind the performances. Between the confident stages, unexpected throwbacks and slightly chaotic fan interactions, the night had a little bit of everything.
 A Setlist Full of Favourites 
 Of course, the music was the main event! Tracks like IZNA and Mamma Mia brought plenty of attitude and energy, while METRONOME and SIGN were the kind of songs that made it difficult to sit still. All four were personal highlights, and hearing them in a concert setting only made their catchy hooks even more satisfying.
 One of the most enjoyable things about the setlist was how much ground it covered. There was room for the group’s bolder, choreography-heavy numbers, but also for songs with a softer or more sentimental feel. Switching between those different moods kept the show from feeling like one long string of similar performances. The girls’ sharp, coordinated movements were a big part of the appeal, but the little smiles and playful exchanges between songs were just as fun to watch.
 Then there was IWALY . For anyone who remembers the girls’ I-LAND 2 journey, this song hits a little differently. Hearing it at their own concert felt like a sweet full-circle moment. What started as part of a survival-show journey has become a song that NAYAs can now sing along to with the group on tour. It was easily one of my favourites of the night, and a lovely way to appreciate just how far izna have come.
 An SNSD Throwback? Yes, Please! 
 The unit stages were another treat, giving the members a chance to try two very different concepts. Mai, Sarang and Saebi took on Girls’ Generation ‘s Kissing You , while Jeemin, Koko and Jungeun delivered their own version of aespa ‘s Illusion . Sweet and playful on one side, cool and charismatic on the other. There really was something for everyone.
 As a huge SNSD fan myself, I was especially excited for Kissing You . Seeing a newer generation of idols perform such an iconic second-generation K-pop song was a wonderful little throwback. The song’s cheerful energy suited the trio, and it was genuinely fun to see them put their own spin on something so familiar. For a few minutes, my inner SONE was having just as good a time as the NAYAs around me!
 Illusion , meanwhile, offered a completely different change of pace. It gave the other three members a chance to lean into a stronger concept, which made the contrast between the two unit stages even more entertaining. Instead of repeating what fans had already seen in the main setlist, the covers showed another side of what the members could do.
 Singapore Slang, Local Food and a Little 6–7 
 The girls certainly did their Singapore homework too! During their talking segments, the members chatted about the local food they had tried, including cereal prawns and chilli crab and really, a visit to Singapore would not be complete without a conversation about food, would it? 
 They also showed off some Singlish, with common words like ‘shiok’ and ‘swee lah’ making an appearance. The newest addition to their vocabulary? ‘Chiobu’! Watching the members learn and play around with local expressions was delightful, especially when the crowd was more than happy to react to every attempt. Consider this their unofficial crash course in Singaporean slang.
 No night with K-pop idols is complete without a little internet humour, the girls even joined in on the viral ‘6–7’ challenge. It was one of those wonderfully random moments that had nothing to do with perfect choreography or polished stages, but was all the more entertaining for it. Sometimes the silly things are exactly what fans remember after a concert.
 The Singapore-specific surprises did not stop there. Jungeun also performed a short rendition of Stefanie Sun ‘s Green Light , a thoughtful nod to the local audience. Hearing a familiar Singaporean song at a K-pop concert was a nice touch and helped make this tour stop feel like more than just another date on the schedule.
 A Sea of Lightsticks and a Few Tears 
 There was plenty of love coming from the audience as well. NAYAs filled Capitol Theatre with cheers, sing-alongs and enthusiastic fanchants, and a coordinated lightstick wave brought fans across both levels together. For a moment, the whole theatre became part of the show. It is always nice when the crowd gets to do more than just watch, and this was a simple but memorable way to bring everyone into the fun.
 The mood turned more emotional towards the end of the concert when Sarang began to cry while sharing her feelings about the performance. She admitted that there were parts she wished she could have done better and that she wanted to return as an even better performer. It was a surprisingly vulnerable moment after a night filled with so much laughter and energy.
 From the audience, it was touching to see how seriously she took the show, even when the fans had been cheering her and the rest of izna on throughout the night. Rather than taking away from the performance, her words made the evening feel more sincere. It was a reminder that behind every carefully rehearsed stage are six young artists who genuinely want to do their best for the people supporting them.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by (x)clusive (@sgxclusive) 
 Up Close and Personal with NAYAs! 
 Just when it seemed like the night was winding down, the members had one more surprise in store. Near the end of the concert, they came down from the stage and made their way around the audience area, interacting with fans up close. For those lucky enough to be along their path, the distance between idol and fan suddenly went from several rows of seats to just a few steps!
 It was a particularly lovely moment at Capitol Theatre, where the concert already felt more intimate than a large arena show. Seeing the girls move around the venue, acknowledge fans and share those brief face-to-face interactions added a personal touch that even the most exciting stage performance cannot quite replicate. Not everyone gets the same view at a concert, of course, but moments like these make the whole experience feel that much more special. It was a concert that showed off both their polished performance side and the fun, earnest personalities that have won over NAYAs.
 Until Next Time, izna! 
 For a group still relatively early in its career, izna has already found a nice balance between confident performances and genuine fan connection. Their first Singapore headlining concert was a reminder that the most memorable parts of a show are not always the biggest or flashiest ones. Sometimes, it is an old favourite, a silly challenge, a local song or a heartfelt message that stays with you.
 And with IZNA , Mamma Mia , METRONOME , SIGN and IWALY still playing in my head, I certainly would not mind doing it all over again. Singapore NAYAs, here’s hoping we get another date with izna soon!
